The whole map built as a giant keyboard — rows and columns of raised keys on a flat base, big enough to run across, with a route weaving between them

layout_placement.text: The keys themselves as press pads — stand on or press a key to take money, packed densely enough that you are always on one
A pad at the far end of the last bank of keys that trades progress for a permanent multiplier

mechanics: Press the buttons to take the money
Buy speed with the money
Get past the obstacles once you are fast enough
notes: Classified Simulation on the '+1 speed' rule rather than Puzzle: the keyboard escape is the activity, but the number going up is the game, so it is Stat Grinder on tier-ladder and it stays P0. Naming Obby or Puzzle second would import a P6 this build does not need.
The keyboard shape is dressing over the tier ladder — banks of keys standing in for tiers — and rides as free text, since no catalogue shape is 'the map is shaped like an object'.
trigger-rebirth is the preset's; the prompt names no rebirth.
Prompt is in Arabic; the reading is a keyboard-shaped map with pressable keys that pay out, speed bought with the takings, and obstacles passed once fast enough.

constraints.text: وبدي الماب يكون كبير — I want the map to be big

open_questions.ask: You want the map big — what's the smallest thing you want to be able to make out on it, the letters on individual keys, whole keys and the shop, or just the banks of keys and the routes between them?
What are the obstacles you get past with speed — walls that only open at a speed, gaps too wide to jump slowly, or something chasing you?
Is the keyboard one flat board you run across, or do the keys step upward so you climb as you progress?
Is the speed shop a building on the keyboard, a pad you stand on, or bought straight from the keys?

captured: a map shaped like a keyboard

notes_for_us: The '+1 speed' rule did its job — this prompt reads as a Puzzle keyboard map on the surface and the note in Simulation names that exact disguise. Worth keeping.

There is no way to say 'the map is shaped like a real-world object'. A keyboard-shaped map, a map shaped like a country, a map shaped like a logo are all the same request and all of them survive only as a sentence in image_prompt. The shape catalogue is about topology, and this is silhouette.
The prompt is not in English. Nothing in the skill says whether text fields should carry the user's own words in their language or a translation; I translated and kept the original in the constraint.

unmatched_options.text: the map should be big and in the shape of a keyboard

skill_gap.name: no map-silhouette option
skill_gap.why: the whole request is that the map's outline is a keyboard; shapes describe topology and options describe features, so an object-shaped map can only be said in free text
